message.content:
Nxeon is a VPS/game-server hosting platform (Next.js 15 app, Postgres via Prisma, marketing pages under app/(marketing)/). You must do ALL your work inside /opt/nxeon-agent-seo — this is a pre-prepared git worktree on its own branch (agent-seo-pages), completely separate from the main /opt/nxeon working tree which another process is actively using concurrently. Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon itself. cd into /opt/nxeon-agent-seo first and stay there for everything (reads, edits, tsc, tests). node_modules and .env are already symlinked in for you. When done, commit your work there (to the existing agent-seo-pages branch — do NOT create a different branch, do NOT merge to main, do NOT push, do NOT run any deploy script) and report back the summary. IMPORTANT: never run `git add -A` or `git add .` in this worktree — node_modules is a symlink and a broad add can stage it in a way that corrupts the real one elsewhere; always `git add` specific files by name.

Two concrete build tasks:

**Task 1 — audit + fill the gap in per-game SEO marketing pages.**
The full game catalog lives in lib/games.ts (look for GAME_FAMILIES / GAME_DISPLAY or similar exports — read the file to find the authoritative list of every game family Nxeon currently sells hosting for). Find where per-game marketing/landing pages actually live (grep app/(marketing)/ for existing game-specific pages — there is very likely an existing pattern/template already used for most games, e.g. a dynamic route or individual page files). Cross-reference: which games in the catalog have NO dedicated marketing/landing page yet? For every game missing one, build a new page following the EXACT existing template/pattern/design system used by the other game pages already in the codebase (don't invent a new design — match what's there, reuse existing components). Read at least 2-3 existing game marketing pages fully before writing new ones so the new pages are indistinguishable in quality/structure from the existing ones. Look for a memory/doc file mentioning "the proven content template" for SEO pages if referenced anywhere in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md or CLAUDE.md — follow it if it exists.

**Task 2 — new regional marketing pages for the new Germany/Europe presence.**
Nxeon recently added a second real hosting region: Falkenstein, Germany (Hetzner, node region code "fsn1" — see lib/node-regions.ts), alongside its existing Singapore region ("sgp1"). Prior to this, all marketing was presumably Singapore/Asia-focused (check existing location-based marketing pages — grep for "Singapore" in app/(marketing)/ and check lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts if it exists, which may already have a pattern for location-based SEO pages). Build new SEO-focused marketing pages for "Germany VPS/game server hosting" and "Europe VPS/game server hosting", following whatever existing location-page template/pattern the codebase already has (check locationLandings.ts and any existing Singapore-focused page). These should be genuinely useful, accurate SEO content (real latency/location claims only — Nxeon's actual regions are Singapore and Falkenstein, Germany, nothing else; never claim other regions/cities that don't exist).

For both tasks: check DOCUMENTATION.md and CLAUDE.md at the repo root first for any established content conventions, brand voice rules (there's a known rule: never imply a 3rd-party infrastructure provider exists to customers — Nxeon speaks as the owner, not as a reseller, even though it uses OVH/Hetzner infrastructure under the hood), or SEO conventions before writing new copy. Run `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and the existing test suite (`npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts`) before considering the work done, and make sure you haven't introduced new failures beyond whatever pre-existing baseline you find when you start (check the failure count BEFORE your changes vs after, via git stash comparison, to confirm you haven't regressed anything). Note: a pre-existing baseline of ~35 unrelated failures (billing/pricing/auth tests) is already known and expected — don't try to fix those, just confirm your changes don't ADD to that count.

Report back with: which games got new pages, what the two new regional pages cover, and confirmation that typecheck + tests are clean (or unchanged from baseline).

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.
17	
18	- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
19	  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
20	  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
21	  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).
22	
23	- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
24	  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
25	  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
26	  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).
27	
28	- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
29	  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
30	  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
31	  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
32	  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
33	  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
34	  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
35	  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.
36	
37	- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
38	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
39	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).
40	
41	## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session
42	
43	`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.
44	
45	1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
46	2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
47	3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
48	4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
49	5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.
50	
51	If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).
52	
53	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
54	
55	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
56	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
57	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
58	
59	## Conventions
60	
61	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
62	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
63	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
64	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
65	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
66	- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
67	- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.
68	
69	## Documentation — keep it current (required)
70	
71	- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
72	- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
73	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
74	- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.
75	
76	## Commands
77	
78	- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
79	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
80	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
81	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
82	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
83	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
84	
85	## Domains & TLS
86	
87	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
88	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
89	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
90	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
91	
92	## Environments
93	
94	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
95	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
96	- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
97	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
98	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.
99	
100	## Safety rules
101	
102	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
103	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
104	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
105	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
106	- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
107	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
108	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.
109

## Multi-node rollout — going from one Proxmox host to two (2026-09-05)

### Motivation and timeline

Nxeon ran on a single Proxmox compute node (the primary, OVH, confirmed via `geoip-lite` against its
live public IP to genuinely be in **Singapore**, not the `bhs`/Canada guess an env-var default had
suggested — always verify a datacenter claim against the live IP, never trust an inferred default) from
launch until 2026-09-05, when a Hetzner server auction listing (#3068915 — i7-8700, 64GB RAM, 2×476.9GB
NVMe, 1×1.92TB SATA SSD, Falkenstein/Germany, one included IPv4 + a routed IPv6 /64) was purchased to
start a European presence. Same day: schema + admin dashboards generalized for multiple nodes, the
physical box installed and onboarded as `node-2`, then a full platform audit (prompted by the owner
asking "the primary node needs to be able to have complete control of all of the nodes, complete
sync — am I right?") found the rollout needed to go further than "the code runs on two nodes" — see
"What the audit found" below. `node-2` was deliberately kept `enabled: false` in the DB through most of
this work; zero real customers were ever provisioned onto it during the entire rollout.

### Schema changes

- `enum NodeProvider { OVH HETZNER }` — a real enum (unlike `Node.region`, a validated plain string —
  see `lib/node-regions.ts`'s `NODE_REGIONS`/`REGION_LABELS`/`REGION_COUNTRY`), because a new
  infrastructure provider is a rare, deliberate business event while datacenter codes grow far more
  often, matching this schema's existing convention (`StaffGrant.area` uses the same "string,
  validated in code" pattern for the same reason).
- `Node.provider`, `Node.region` (default `"sgp1"` for the primary, confirmed Singapore per above),
  `Node.providerServerId` (the provider's own identifier for the box — OVH's "service name" or
  Hetzner's server number — distinct from `pveNode`, needed by the per-node dedicated-IP branch).
- `DedicatedIp.nodeId` (required, FK to `Node`) — added nullable, backfilled every existing row to the
  primary's id, then tightened to `NOT NULL` with the FK constraint, all in one hand-reviewed manual
  migration (`prisma/manual-migrations/2026-09-05-node-provider-region.sql`) rather than two separate
  `db push` rounds — production has real `DedicatedIp` rows, and `prisma db push` cannot auto-populate
  a new required relation column against non-empty data (confirmed live: `promote-production.sh`'s
  usual `db push --accept-data-loss` refused with "you may use --force-reset... all data will be lost"
  on this exact migration, precisely because 9 real rows existed — the manual-migration-file convention
  this repo already uses for schema changes exists for exactly this scenario, and paid off immediately).
- Contrast with `HostingNode` (the separate shared-hosting product's node model): `HostingNode` has
  `sshHost`/`sshPort`/`rootPasswordEnc` because that product's trust model is direct SSH to each box;
  `Node` deliberately has no SSH fields, only a scoped Proxmox API token (`apiUrl`/`tokenId`/
  `tokenSecret`) — a real, deliberate difference in security posture between the two products, not an
  oversight to "fix" by adding SSH fields to `Node`.

### Hetzner API client + dedicated-IP generalization

`lib/hetzner.ts` (new) mirrors `lib/ovh.ts`'s shape but reflects real wire-format differences: HTTP
Basic Auth (not OVH's signed AK/AS/CK headers), form-urlencoded bodies (not JSON), and additional IPs
route straight to the server's real MAC with a **per-IP gateway read from Hetzner's own API response**
(not a fixed `.254`-of-the-/24 formula like OVH, and no "Virtual MAC" object to create/poll/delete).
`hetznerApi.orderAdditionalIp()` is a deliberate stub that throws "not implemented" — the exact Robot
API endpoint for a real, paid IP-ordering transaction could not be confirmed from available
documentation, and this is not something to guess at for an endpoint that spends real money.
`lib/dedicated-ip.ts` was rewritten to resolve a `Node` row and branch by `provider` per call
(`resolveNode`, `dedicatedIpProviderConfigured`, `syncOvhPool`/`syncHetznerPool`) instead of one
hardcoded OVH server constant — additive; every existing importer that never passes a `nodeId` still
resolves to the primary, unchanged.

### Per-server Proxmox correctness fixes (Step 4)

Multiple customer/staff/Discord-bot surfaces called bare Proxmox singleton functions
(`vmStatus`/`listSnapshots`/`listBackups`) bound to the primary's env-derived credentials regardless of
which node a server actually lives on — harmless with one node (nothing to route to *wrong*), a real
"customer sees another tenant's VM stats" bug the instant a second node has real traffic, since vmids
are not globally unique across physical hosts. Fixed in `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`,
`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, `lib/discord-status-command.ts`, `app/api/servers/[id]/backups/
download/route.ts`, and `lib/actions-server-ops.ts`, all routing through a new `pveForNode(node)`
helper in `lib/proxmox.ts`. (The much larger, platform-wide version of this same bug class — SSH/RCON
connection resolution, not just Proxmox API calls — is covered under "What the audit found" below; this
Step-4 fix only covered the Proxmox-API half.)

### Admin dashboards + deploy wizard (Steps 5, 7)

`app/admin/monitoring/page.tsx` (VM table + node-metrics chart), `app/admin/page.tsx` (fleet health
summary), and `app/admin/infrastructure/page.tsx` (per-node cards) were redesigned to loop every
enabled `Node` instead of showing only the primary's numbers — `lib/monitoring.ts`'s `nodeTargets()`/
`nodeRamUsage()`/`nodeStorageUsage()` already had the right multi-node shape from earlier work and
needed no changes; the dashboards just needed to actually call them instead of the bare singletons.
Added `nodeStatus`/`listVms`/`storageStatus`/`nodeRrd` optional-`conn` parameters to `lib/proxmox.ts`
(mirroring `vmRrd`'s existing pattern) so these could be called per-node. `components/admin/NodeForms.tsx`,
`app/admin/nodes/page.tsx`/`[id]/page.tsx`, and the customer deploy wizard's location picker
(`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx`) got Provider/Region fields and badges — the customer-facing
picker deliberately shows only a country flag + region name (`lib/flag-emoji.ts` → later replaced with
an image-based `components/ui/CountryFlag.tsx` once Unicode regional-indicator emoji turned out not to
render as flags on all platforms, notably Windows), never the provider name or raw IP — matching the
standing brand rule that Nxeon never surfaces a third-party infrastructure provider to customers.

### The physical install (kept verbatim from the original entry)

Nxeon's second compute node (`node-2`, Hetzner auction server #3068915, Falkenstein, `nxeon-fsn1`,
178.63.94.114) was onboarded using the standard "install via QEMU inside Hetzner's rescue system"
technique: boot into Hetzner rescue, download the official Proxmox VE ISO, bake an automated-install
`answer.toml` into it with `proxmox-auto-install-assistant`, then boot that ISO under
`qemu-system-x86_64` with the real physical disks passed through directly (`-drive file=/dev/nvme0n1`
etc., emulated as `-device nvme` so the guest sees the same `nvme0n1`/`nvme1n1` names the answer file's
`disk-list` references), so the installer partitions the actual hardware. When it finishes, reboot the
physical host out of rescue mode into the fresh install.

2	 *  from server components and "use server" action files alike). */
3	export const GAME_FAMILIES = ["minecraft", "valheim", "rust", "palworld", "cs2", "terraria", "ark", "satisfactory", "projectzomboid", "sdtd", "vrising", "enshrouded", "factorio", "gmod", "conan", "unturned", "theforest", "sonsoftheforest", "bedrock", "schedule1", "dragonwilds", "sunkenland", "abioticfactor", "corekeeper", "icarus", "arkasa", "soulmask", "dst", "vintagestory", "necesse", "tf2", "l4d2", "nightingale", "squad", "spaceengineers", "kf2", "barotrauma", "sandstorm", "mordhau", "theisle", "stationeers", "eco", "empyrion", "plutoniumt4", "plutoniumt5", "plutoniumt6", "plutoniumiw5"] as const;
4	export type GameFamily = (typeof GAME_FAMILIES)[number];

6	/**
7	 * Canonical display name + glyph per family, ALL 19 — the single source of truth
8	 * for capitalization (e.g. "Garry's Mod", "7 Days to Die", "ARK: Survival
9	 * Evolved", never a raw lowercase slug). Plain module, so unlike
10	 * components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx's GAME_VISUAL (which is "use client" and
11	 * also carries brand gradient colors) this is safe to import from a SERVER
12	 * component too.
13	 *
14	 * FIXED 2026-08-23: the deploy wizard's game picker (app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx)
15	 * and the "manage my servers" list (app/dashboard/games/page.tsx) each kept their
16	 * OWN copy-pasted map with only 6 of 19 games — every other family silently fell
17	 * back to its raw slug ("sdtd", "gmod", "theforest"...) with no capitalization at
18	 * all. Both now import this instead of maintaining their own list.
19	 */

82	  //    2026-08-31 (prisma/seed-wave9-games.ts). All five have real, currently-
83	  //    shipping dedicated server support confirmed against SteamDB/official
84	  //    docs — see that file's header comment for App IDs and Docker images. ──
85	  mordhau: { name: "Mordhau", glyph: "⚔️" },
86	  theisle: { name: "The Isle", glyph: "🦕" },

103	  plutoniumt4: { name: "Plutonium T4 (WaW)", glyph: "🛰️" },
104	  // T5/T6/IW5 added 2026-08-31 alongside T4 — see prisma/seed-plutonium.ts's
105	  // header for the full research and safety rules shared by this whole family.
106	  plutoniumt5: { name: "Plutonium T5 (BO1)", glyph: "🛰️" },
107	  plutoniumt6: { name: "Plutonium T6 (BO2)", glyph: "🛰️" },

111	/**
112	 * Family id → art slug for the real key-art bundled at
113	 * public/games/art/<slug>_poster.jpg and public/games/art/<slug>_hero.jpg
114	 * (naming differs from the family id for a few titles). Single source of truth
115	 * for every consumer (GameCoverCarousel, GameCoverTile, GameHero) — was
116	 * previously copy-pasted separately in GameCoverCarousel.tsx, which is exactly
117	 * the kind of drift that caused the GAME_DISPLAY capitalization bug above.
118	 *
119	 * Every family has both a `hero` and a `poster`; a `poster` is only ever
120	 * omitted for a family whose cover art has not been produced yet (a scaffolded
121	 * family), in which case consumers fall back through their own chain.
122	 */
123	/**
124	 * Family id → the port a customer's game client actually connects to, plus
125	 * which transport it is reachable on. This is the single source of truth for
126	 * `worker/provision-health.ts`'s post-boot game-port verification (added after
127	 * a Terraria order silently sat on an interactive world-selection prompt with
128	 * no TTY — the container showed "Up" while nothing ever bound the port, and
129	 * PROVISION reported success anyway).
130	 *
131	 * SOURCED DIRECTLY from each family's `docker run -p ...` mapping in
132	 * prisma/catalog.ts / prisma/seed-wave1-games.ts / prisma/seed-wave2-games.ts —
133	 * these are the ONLY ports Docker actually exposes off the container, so they
134	 * are the only ports reachable from outside it. If a game's setup script ever
135	 * changes its `-p` mapping, this entry must change with it or the health check
136	 * will probe a port nothing forwards to.
137	 *
138	 * `protocol` is not always the game's own play port: several titles (valheim,
139	 * palworld, vrising, enshrouded, theforest, sonsoftheforest, bedrock) expose
140	 * ONLY a UDP port in their image — no TCP port is mapped at all, so there is
141	 * nothing a TCP connect could ever prove for them. Where an image also exposes
142	 * a TCP port (often RCON/query, e.g. rust's 28016, ark's 27020, factorio's
143	 * 27015) THAT port is used instead: a TCP handshake is verifiable with a plain
144	 * connect, and the process binding it is proof the game server itself came up,
145	 * which is exactly the class of bug this check exists to catch — even though
146	 * it isn't the port the player's game client uses to join.
147	 */
148	export const GAME_PORT: Record<GameFamily, { port: number; protocol: "tcp" | "udp" }> = {
149	  minecraft: { port: 25565, protocol: "tcp" },
150	  valheim: { port: 2456, protocol: "udp" }, // no tcp port mapped
151	  rust: { port: 28016, protocol: "tcp" }, // rcon tcp; 28015/udp is the join port
152	  palworld: { port: 8211, protocol: "udp" }, // no tcp port mapped
153	  cs2: { port: 27015, protocol: "tcp" },
154	  terraria: { port: 7777, protocol: "tcp" },
155	  ark: { port: 27020, protocol: "tcp" }, // rcon tcp; 7777/7778/27015 are udp
156	  satisfactory: { port: 7777, protocol: "tcp" }, // image maps 7777 as both tcp+udp
157	  projectzomboid: { port: 27015, protocol: "tcp" }, // rcon tcp; 16261/16262 are udp
158	  sdtd: { port: 26900, protocol: "tcp" }, // 26900 is mapped as both tcp+udp
159	  vrising: { port: 9876, protocol: "udp" }, // no tcp port mapped
160	  // Enshrouded is SINGLE-PORT: the current dedicated server binds only its
161	  // queryPort. Verified live 2026-09-07 on a fully-started server — its own
162	  // generated `enshrouded_server.json` carries a `queryPort` key and NO
163	  // `gamePort` key at all, the process bound udp:15637 and nothing on 15636,
164	  // and an A2S_INFO datagram to 15637 answered `ff ff ff ff 41 …` while 15636
165	  // was silent. The old 15636 here (the pre-2024 two-port scheme) meant the
166	  // provisioning health check probed a port nothing ever binds, so EVERY
167	  // Enshrouded order sat in "Installing the game…" for 45 minutes per attempt

253	/**
254	 * The families whose {@link GAME_PORT} entry is deliberately NOT the port a
255	 * player's own game client connects to — mapped to the port that actually is.
256	 *
257	 * `GAME_PORT` is a HEALTH-CHECK map. Where an image exposes a TCP port at all it
258	 * prefers that one, because "a TCP handshake is verifiable with a plain connect,
259	 * and the process binding it is proof the game server itself came up" — see its
260	 * own comment. For most families that port is also the join port, so the
261	 * distinction never mattered. For the eight below it is an RCON/query/admin
262	 * port, and `GAME_PORT`'s own inline comments have always said so.
263	 *
264	 * It started mattering the moment provisioning began auto-forwarding "the game's
265	 * own port" for NAT servers using this same map. Found live 2026-09-06 by
266	 * provisioning a real Rust server on node-2: the guest listened correctly on
267	 * 28015/udp (join) and 28016/tcp (RCON), the node's NAT had exactly one game
268	 * rule — 28016/tcp — and the dashboard handed the customer that RCON port as
269	 * their connect address. No player could ever have joined. That is the identical
270	 * outage found on the real paying customer `rust-w75hko` (see
271	 * docs/DOCUMENTATION.md's node migration section), whose root cause was
272	 * previously read as "allocateGameForward was never called for it"; it is called,
273	 * just with the wrong port.
274	 *
275	 * Every entry is sourced from the family's own `docker run -p ...` mapping in
276	 * prisma/catalog.ts / the seed-wave*-games.ts files — the only ports docker
277	 * actually exposes off the container — cross-checked against the join port
278	 * `GAME_PORT`'s own comment already names. Anything NOT listed here joins on its
279	 * `GAME_PORT` entry; use {@link joinPortFor} rather than reading this directly.
280	 */
281	const GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE: Partial<Record<GameFamily, { port: number; protocol: "tcp" | "udp" }>> = {
282	  rust: { port: 28015, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 28016/tcp rcon
283	  ark: { port: 7777, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 27020/tcp rcon
284	  projectzomboid: { port: 16261, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 27015/tcp rcon
285	  factorio: { port: 34197, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 27015/tcp rcon
286	  arkasa: { port: 7777, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 27020/tcp rcon
287	  // (soulmask needs no entry any more: its GAME_PORT is now 8777/udp — the port
288	  //  players join on — because its 18888/tcp admin port turned out to be bound
289	  //  to loopback inside the container and unreachable. See GAME_PORT.)
290	  squad: { port: 7787, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 21114/tcp rcon
291	  kf2: { port: 7777, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 8080/tcp webadmin
292	  // Source-engine families: srcds binds the SAME port number on both protocols,
293	  // and the two are different services. UDP 27015 is the game + A2S query
294	  // protocol players and server browsers speak; TCP 27015 is RCON. Proven live
295	  // on a running Garry's Mod server 2026-09-07 — an A2S_INFO datagram to UDP
296	  // 27015 answered `ff ff ff ff 41 …` (S2C_CHALLENGE), while TCP 27015 accepted
297	  // the connection and returned nothing at all to the same query. Because the
298	  // port NUMBERS match, this one hid where the others didn't: the forward looked
299	  // right and was on the wrong protocol, so players could not connect AND the
300	  // single port left published to the internet was RCON — the exact exposure
301	  // `196e5c9` was written to end.
302	  gmod: { port: 27015, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 27015/tcp rcon
303	  // 7 Days to Die is the same shape as the Source families above — it binds
304	  // 26900 on BOTH protocols and only the UDP one carries the game. Verified
305	  // live 2026-09-07: the server's own log says `[NET] Disabling protocol:
306	  // SteamNetworking` then `NET: LiteNetLib server started`, and LiteNetLib is
307	  // UDP-only; an A2S_INFO datagram to udp:26900 answered `ff ff ff ff 41 …`
308	  // (S2C_CHALLENGE) while tcp:26900 accepted the connection and replied with
309	  // four unrelated ASCII bytes. Matching port numbers hid this exactly the way
310	  // they hid it for Garry's Mod.
311	  sdtd: { port: 26900, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 26900/tcp
312	  tf2: { port: 27015, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 27015/tcp rcon
313	  l4d2: { port: 27015, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 27015/tcp rcon
314	  cs2: { port: 27015, protocol: "udp" }, // GAME_PORT is 27015/tcp rcon
315	  // (unturned needs no entry: its GAME_PORT is already 27015/udp — the same port
316	  //  players join on — because Unturned binds no TCP port at all. See GAME_PORT.)
317	};

I want to stash both tracked and untracked changes together to get a pure baseline, so I'll use git stash -u to include the new page files, run the baseline checks, then pop the stash back. Though I need to watch out that this could also sweep in node_modules if it's untracked.

Actually that's risky since node_modules is a symlink and stashing it could temporarily remove it from disk, breaking tsc while the stash is active. A safer approach is to use plain git stash to only shelve the tracked modified files, and handle the new untracked page files separately since they're purely additive and shouldn't affect the baseline for other pages anyway.

But wait, if I stash the tracked changes to data.ts, the new pages import fields like PREVIEW_GAMES.squad that would no longer exist, contaminating the baseline with false errors. The cleanest fix is to temporarily move the new page directories out to a scratch location before stashing the tracked modifications.

content.content:
9357	### The structural finding: config-apply exists for five families, not forty-seven
9358	
9359	`worker/game-config.ts`'s `applyRealConfig` switch has exactly five cases —
9360	`minecraft`, `rust`, `valheim`, `cs2`, `palworld`. **Every other family falls through
9361	to the simulated default.** This is worth stating plainly because it is easy to read
9362	`REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES` as a rollout in progress: it is not a per-family verification
9363	backlog, there is simply no implementation to enable for the other forty-two. A
9364	customer changing a setting on any of them gets a success message and no change on
9365	their server.
9366	
9367	### Eco — never started at all, and its join port was TCP for a UDP game (`dc6e07f`)
9368	
9369	Two independent faults, either one fatal:
9370	
9371	1. `emackie/steamcmd-eco`'s entrypoint execs `EcoServer` with no arguments and offers
9372	   no hook to add any, and EcoServer refuses to boot without credentials —
9373	   `"Authentication to Strange Cloud failed. No authentication methods were available
9374	   … or use '-offline'"`, exit 232. Under the provisioning wrapper's systemd unit that
9375	   is a crash loop, caught live at `NRestarts=30`. The entrypoint is now overridden to
9376	   run the image's own steamcmd line and then `EcoServer -offline`.
9377	2. `GAME_PORT.eco` said `3000/tcp`. Read off a running EcoServer's own `/proc/net`:
9378	   `udp:3000` bound, `tcp:3001` (WebServer), `tcp:3002` (RCON), **no `tcp:3000`**.
9379	
9380	**Owner decision:** `-offline` means direct-connect only — not listed in Eco's public
9381	browser. Listing requires the *customer's own paid Eco account* (`-userToken` /
9382	`-username`), which is a question about what the panel collects, not something
9383	provisioning can invent.
9384	
9385	### Garry's Mod — the image tag never contained the game (`b6cf476`)
9386	
9387	`ghcr.io/ich777/steamcmd:garrysmod` is ich777's **template** image. Read straight off
9388	it: `GAME_ID=template`, `GAME_NAME=template`, `GAME_PARAMS=template`. The appid is
9389	meant to be supplied per container. Because the setup script overrode only
9390	`GAME_PARAMS`, the entrypoint ran `+app_update template validate` — a silent no-op,
9391	SteamCMD connects, downloads nothing and exits 0 — so `srcds_run` never existed and
9392	`start-server.sh` died on "No such file or directory". Permanent crash loop, caught at
9393	**`NRestarts=61` with 8.0K in a perfectly writable bind mount**.
9394	
9395	The `seed-wave7-games.ts` comment defended the stale image tag on the grounds that the
9396	binary "is pulled fresh via `+app_update 4020` at every container start". That was an
9397	assumption, and it had never been true. With `GAME_ID=4020` the same container
9398	downloads **6,870,007,094 bytes (6.4 GiB)**.
9399	
9400	### Source-engine families were forwarding RCON instead of the game (`b6cf476`)
9401	
9402	The wider bug found underneath GMod. `srcds` binds the **same port number on both
9403	protocols**, and the two are different services: **UDP 27015 is the game + A2S query
9404	protocol** players and server browsers speak; **TCP 27015 is RCON**. Proven on the
9405	running server — an `A2S_INFO` datagram to UDP 27015 answered
9406	`ff ff ff ff 41 …` (S2C_CHALLENGE), while TCP 27015 accepted the connection and
9407	returned **nothing** to the same query.
9408	
9409	`joinPortFor` had no entry for these families, so provisioning forwarded `27015/tcp`.
9410	Because the port *numbers* match, this hid where `rust`/`ark`/`factorio` did not — the
9411	address on the dashboard looked correct while players could not connect, and the one
9412	port left published to the internet was **RCON**, the exact exposure `196e5c9` was
9413	written to end. `gmod`/`tf2`/`l4d2`/`cs2` now override to `27015/udp`; `GAME_PORT`
9414	deliberately stays TCP for all four, because a TCP connect remains the honest evidence
9415	that srcds bound its ports.
9416	
9417	Verified after deploy by the strongest test available: a real **A2S_INFO query sent
9418	from off-box to `178.63.94.114:20018`** — the public forward — returned a Source
9419	`S2C_CHALLENGE`, which is exactly what a player's server browser does. `tf2` is not yet
9420	confirmed against a real server and remains on the sweep's list.
9421	
9422	### Left 4 Dead 2 — both bind mounts unwritable (`b97d143`)
9423	
9424	`left4devops/l4d2` runs as `uid=1000(louis)`; docker auto-creates a bind mount
9425	`root:root 0755`. Confirmed from inside the running container: `touch: cannot touch
9426	'/addons/.nxw': Permission denied`, and the same for `/cfg`. Same class as
9427	conan/tf2/squad/mordhau, same one-line `chown -R 1000:1000` fix — but it bites harder
9428	here, because this image keeps the game files in the container layer on purpose and
9429	bind-mounts **only** addons and cfg. Those two directories are the entire persistent
9430	surface of a customer's server, and neither is what the health check looks at, so the
9431	server provisions "successfully" and looks fine while nothing a customer does survives.
9432	
9433	### Stationeers cannot be sold today — the image drives a build it no longer matches
9434	
9435	Installs cleanly (13.3 GB into a writable mount, healthy container, no restart loop)
9436	but the game **never binds any port, TCP or UDP**, and never creates a world —
9437	`saves/` stayed empty after 10+ minutes across three configurations.
9438	
9439	`didstopia/stationeers-server`'s `start.sh` always appends `-worldname=X -loadworld=X`
9440	unquoted from image ENV defaults (`STATIONEERS_WORLD_NAME=docker`), and tests them with
9441	`${VAR+x}` (set-or-not), so passing an empty value does not suppress them. Along the
9442	way: the catalog set `STATIONEERS_WORLD_NAME='Nxeon World'` — a value **with a space** —
9443	which the unquoted interpolation split into `-worldname=Nxeon World -loadworld=Nxeon
9444	World`. Fixing that was necessary and still not sufficient; supplying modern
9445	`-settings StartLocalHost true …` still had the legacy flags appended after it and the
9446	container exited 127.
9447	
9448	**This needs the owner**, exactly like CS2's and Conan's: replacing the image (or
9449	writing a full entrypoint override, as was done for Eco above) is a catalog decision,
9450	not a setup-script tweak, and was not guessed at here.
9451	
9452	### Don't Starve Together cannot be sold today — it needs a per-customer Klei token
9453	
9454	The server refuses to start, in its own words:
9455	
9456	```
9457	[200] Account Failed (6): "E_INVALID_TOKEN"
9458	!!!! Your Server Will Not Start !!!!
9459	No auth token could be found.
9460	Please visit https://accounts.klei.com/account/game/servers?game=DontStarveTogether
9461	```
9462	
9463	The setup script passes `-e TOKEN=''`. A DST cluster token is generated from the
9464	*customer's own Klei account*; there is no anonymous or platform-wide equivalent, so
9465	no setup-script change can fix this.
9466	
9467	This also corrects a standing catalog assumption. `seed-wave9-games.ts` groups "DST's
9468	TOKEN" with Dragonwilds' `OWNER_ID` as customer-specific values where "the container
9469	boots and is reachable with sane defaults out of the box, and the customer edits the
9470	mounted config file post-deploy via SFTP". For DST that is **false** — it does not boot
9471	at all. Selling DST requires the panel to collect a Klei cluster token at order time.
9472	
9473	### Smaller findings
9474	
9475	- **Core Keeper advertises the wrong port.** It is joined by Game ID rather than
9476	  IP:port, and its session line reads `178.63.94.114;27015;<id>;<key>` — the *guest*
9477	  port. NAT maps public `20018 -> guest 27015`, so a player following the advertised
9478	  Game ID is sent to a port that is not forwarded. Worth a look for any family that
9479	  publishes its own port to a lobby/relay instead of being handed one.
9480	- **No family passes a Steam Game Server Login Token**, which is what public
9481	  server-browser listing needs. L4D2 logs `[S_API FAIL] SteamAPI_Init() failed` and
9482	  does not answer A2S while hibernating, though its port is bound and reachable.
9483	- **Do not tear down a test VM while its provisioning job is still RUNNING.** Doing so
9484	  wedged the worker's serial job loop against a destroyed guest, and a real customer's
9485	  `BACKUP_CREATE` job sat QUEUED behind it for ~40 minutes until `nxeon-worker` was
9486	  restarted (by unit — never by process pattern). The sweep harness now refuses it.
9487	
9488	**Still unswept** after this pass: `sdtd, enshrouded, theforest, sonsoftheforest,
9489	dragonwilds, sunkenland, abioticfactor, icarus, arkasa, soulmask, vintagestory,
9490	nightingale, squad, spaceengineers, kf2, barotrauma, sandstorm, theisle, empyrion,
9491	tf2` (tf2 needs only the join-port confirmation above).
9492	
9493	---
9494	
9495	*Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md`
9496	(server migration).*

### Blocker 1 — the container cannot write its own bind mounts (FIXED)

`prisma/seed-wave7-games.ts`'s Conan setup script mounted `-v /opt/conan/game:/conanexiles -v
/opt/conan/config:/conanexiles_config` **without creating or chowning either directory first**, so
docker auto-created both as `root:root 0755`. `melle2/conanexiles-ds` runs as `uid=7100(conanexiles)`.
Straight off the running container:

```
wine: '/conanexiles' is not owned by you, refusing to create a configuration directory there
Game not installed.
Start game download...
...
Game download done.
Link config dir /conanexiles/ConanSandbox/nxeon
ln: failed to create symbolic link '/conanexiles/ConanSandbox/nxeon': No such file or directory
```

Then the entrypoint exits, systemd restarts it 5s later, and it does the whole thing again.
Measured on the live VM after ~20 minutes: **`NRestarts=38`**, both bind mounts still `4.0K`, root
filesystem at 17 GB, `docker ps -s` showing a **5.53 GB writable layer** — i.e. every loop was
re-pulling the 5.3 GB game into the container's own layer, where a single `docker rm` would delete it.
The game port never bound, so the provision failed after all three attempts:

```
game port 7777/tcp never opened on 178.63.94.114:20021 after ~306s ... The install stopped making
progress (3 consecutive minutes with no disk growth and no container output, at 17700 MB used)
```

**Fix:** `mkdir -p /opt/conan/game /opt/conan/config && chown -R 7100:7100 /opt/conan` ahead of the
`docker run`, in `prisma/seed-wave7-games.ts` and in the live `OsTemplate` row (same two-place fix as

is the pattern the catalog's other non-root families already use: factorio `chown 845:845`,

## SEO gap-fill — 10 missing per-game landing pages + Germany/Europe regional pages (2026-09-14)

Two audits, done on the `agent-seo-pages` worktree (`/opt/nxeon-agent-seo`) and merged into
`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` here for the record:

**Per-game marketing pages.** Cross-referenced `GAME_FAMILIES` (`lib/games.ts`, 47 families) against
every hand-written `app/(marketing)/*-server-hosting/page.tsx` route. 31 families had a page already;
`schedule1` is correctly excluded (never seeded — no official dedicated server exists). That left 16
families with a real, active `GamePlan` row and no landing page: Nightingale, Squad, Space Engineers,
Killing Floor 2, Barotrauma, Insurgency: Sandstorm, Mordhau, The Isle, Stationeers, Eco, Empyrion (the
Wave 8/9 titles), plus Plutonium T4/T5/T6/IW5.

- **10 new pages shipped**, each built with the same `GameLandingCombined` component, `PreviewGame` data
  shape (`components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`), and FAQ/related-links wrapper every other game page
  already uses — plans/RAM/CPU/slots/prices copied verbatim from the live `GamePlan` table, boot-sequence
  ports sourced from each family's real `joinPortsFor()` result (`lib/games.ts`). `GAME_VISUAL` in
  `components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx` gained matching brand-gradient entries for all 11 Wave 8/9 families
  (they were missing there too, falling through to the generic grey "🎮 Game" tile everywhere the badge
  renders, not just on a dedicated page). `app/sitemap.ts` got a new entry per page.
- **Stationeers was deliberately excluded** despite having a real `GamePlan` row: this same document's
  "Stationeers cannot be sold today" finding above (2026-09-07 sweep) confirmed live that
  `didstopia/stationeers-server` never binds a port or creates a world. Building a dedicated SEO page
  would have actively driven paid signups to a product confirmed not to start — it still shows on
  `/game-servers` today (unrelated to this change), but gets no landing page until that's fixed. Flagged
  separately for the owner/ops rather than shipped around.
- **Plutonium T4/T5/T6/IW5 were also excluded** — a bigger, separate discovery made while sourcing real
  prices for the 10 pages above: `app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx`'s "Specialty & community
  servers" section advertises "from $5.99–$6.99/mo" for all four and links to `/plutonium-t4-hosting`
  etc., but a direct query against the live `GamePlan` table found **zero rows for any of the four** —
  no seed file for them exists in `prisma/` despite several comments elsewhere in this codebase referring
  to a `prisma/seed-plutonium.ts` that isn't actually present. The four links are also already present in
  `app/sitemap.ts`, meaning Google is being pointed at four pages that don't exist, advertising prices
  for plans that don't exist. Pre-existing, not touched here; flagged for a follow-up session (needs a
  real pricing decision + a real seed file, not a guess).
- Two more pre-existing "cannot be sold" families surfaced by the same read of this doc's own sweep
  history — **Conan Exiles** ("Blocker 2 — the server binary itself never starts, OWNER DECISION") and
  **CS2** ("cannot be provisioned at all, on any plan") — already have live marketing pages predating
  this change; left as-is (out of scope for a page-gap-fill), but new cross-links from the pages built
  here were kept off both games on purpose.

**Germany + Europe regional pages.** `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` gained a new `LocationDef`,
`"germany"` (`presence: "datacenter"`) — Nxeon's real second production node, Hetzner Falkenstein
(`fsn1`, onboarded 2026-09-05, see the "Multi-node rollout" section above), marketed as "Germany" per
`lib/node-regions.ts`'s existing `CUSTOMER_REGION_LABELS` convention (the small-town name confuses
customers, so the region picker already shows "Germany" there — this page does the same). The `"europe"`
`RegionDef` was flipped from `presence: "market"` to `"datacenter"` and now includes `"germany"` in its
`locationSlugs`, alongside the existing London/Frankfurt/Amsterdam/Paris market pages. Because the
programmatic `(location) × (service)` matrix in that file drives `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx`, this
alone brings 12 new indexable pages live with zero new route files: `/germany-vps-hosting`,
`/germany-game-server-hosting`, `/germany-web-hosting`, `/germany-dedicated-server-hosting`,
`/germany-forex-vps-hosting`, `/germany-reseller-hosting`, and the `/europe-*` equivalents of each
(`sitemap.ts` already loops `LANDING_SLUGS`/`REGION_LANDING_SLUGS`, so no sitemap edit was needed here).

- **Found and fixed a real accuracy bug while wiring this up**: `regionServerLocationFaq()` hardcoded the
  literal string "Singapore" (and "Singapore VPS Hosting") into its "does Nxeon actually have a
  datacenter here" answer, because Asia-Pacific was the only `presence: "datacenter"` region when that
  function was written. Flipping Europe to `"datacenter"` without fixing this would have made the new
  `/europe-*-hosting` pages tell readers Nxeon's datacenter is "physically located in Singapore, inside
  Europe" — false, and exactly the kind of fabricated location claim this file's own honesty doctrine
  exists to prevent. Fixed to resolve the real datacenter city and the calling page's own service label
  dynamically instead of hardcoding either. The non-datacenter branch's "runs from a Singapore datacenter
  today" was similarly stale (true but incomplete) and now names both real datacenters.

resolved back to 35 on immediate re-run with no code change, consistent with flakiness against the live,
concurrently-used `nxeon` database rather than anything in this change).
